what_its_for: Ramelteon helps you fall asleep if you have trouble getting to sleep at night. It works by mimicking a natural hormone in your body called melatonin, which tells your brain it is time to sleep. Unlike some other sleep medicines, ramelteon is not habit-forming.
how_to_take: Take ramelteon by mouth as a whole tablet with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet. Take it within 30 minutes of going to bed. Only take it when you are ready to go to sleep and have at least 7 to 8 hours available before you need to wake up. Do NOT take it with or right after eating a heavy or high-fat meal, as food can slow down how well the medicine works.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is 8 mg (one tablet) taken once a night, about 30 minutes before bedtime. Do not take more than one dose per night. Your doctor will tell you the right dose for you. Do not take extra doses to try to fall asleep faster.
missed_dose: Ramelteon is only taken when needed at bedtime, so a missed dose is not a concern the way it is with daily medicines. Simply skip the missed dose and take your next dose the following night at bedtime if needed. Never take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store ramelteon at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it in its original container, away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Safely dispose of any unused or expired medicine through a medicine take-back program or by following your pharmacist's instructions.
what_to_avoid: Avoid alcohol while taking ramelteon, as combining them can cause dangerous drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid eating a large or high-fat meal right before taking ramelteon. Do not take fluvoxamine (Luvox) with ramelteon, as this combination can cause serious side effects — tell your doctor about ALL medicines you take. Avoid smoking, as it may reduce how well ramelteon works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: unusual behaviors while sleeping such as sleepwalking, sleep-driving, or doing other activities while not fully awake; worsening depression or thoughts of hurting yourself; allergic reactions such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe dizziness or fainting; changes in your menstrual cycle, unexpected milk production from your breasts, or decreased sex drive (these may be signs of a hormone problem); or if your sleep problems do not improve after 7 to 10 days of treatment.
when_it_works: Ramelteon usually starts to help you fall asleep within 30 minutes of taking it. You may notice improvement in your sleep from the very first night, but it may take a few nights of use to see the full benefit. If your sleep does not improve after about one to two weeks, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and falls. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine. Children and teenagers: Ramelteon is not approved for use in children or teenagers under 18 years old. Liver problems: Do not take ramelteon if you have severe liver disease. Tell your doctor about any liver problems before starting this medicine.
